Chapter Overview

Bagian ini menjadi pintu masuk. Bacalah situasi awal dan pahami arah belajar bab ini.

Welcome to Chapter 6

Dalam bab ini, kamu akan belajar menggunakan Bahasa Inggris untuk membahas isu penting dalam kehidupan remaja: money, online shopping, digital wallets, and digital scams. Kamu akan belajar cara menyampaikan pendapat, memberikan alasan, membangun argumen, membaca teks analytical exposition, berdiskusi, dan menulis esai pendek tentang penggunaan dompet digital di kalangan pelajar.

Tema ini dekat dengan kehidupan sehari-hari. Banyak remaja menggunakan uang jajan untuk membeli makanan, kuota internet, alat tulis, pulsa, atau barang online. Di daerah kepulauan, keputusan membeli sesuatu kadang lebih rumit karena ongkos kirim bisa mahal, pengiriman bisa lama, dan jaringan internet tidak selalu stabil.

Situational Hook

Imagine this situation.

A student sees a pair of earphones online. The price is only Rp25,000. He thinks, “Wow, this is cheap!” However, when he checks the shipping cost to his island, the total price becomes Rp62,000. The seller has only two reviews, and one buyer says the item arrived broken. At the same time, the student only has Rp50,000 for one week. He still needs to buy internet data and a notebook for school.

What should he do? Should he buy it because it looks cheap, or save the money for school needs?

Big Idea 1

Teenagers need financial literacy.
Remaja perlu mengelola uang, membedakan kebutuhan dan keinginan, serta membuat keputusan finansial yang bijak.

Big Idea 2

Online shopping can be useful but risky.
Belanja online bisa membantu, tetapi siswa perlu memperhatikan harga, ongkir, ulasan toko, dan keamanan transaksi.

Big Idea 3

Digital wallets have benefits and disadvantages.
Dompet digital memudahkan pembayaran, tetapi dapat mendorong pengeluaran impulsif.

Big Idea 4

A strong argument needs clear reasons and evidence.
Argumen yang kuat harus punya alasan, contoh, dan penjelasan.

  • menyampaikan pendapat tentang literasi keuangan remaja;
  • memberi alasan menggunakan causal conjunctions;

Writing and Presenting

What Is Analytical Exposition Text?

Analytical exposition membantumu menyampaikan opini secara masuk akal, bukan sekadar berkata “I agree” atau “I disagree”.

Definition

Analytical exposition text is a text that presents the writer’s opinion about an issue and supports it with arguments.

Teks analytical exposition adalah teks yang menyampaikan pendapat penulis tentang suatu isu dan mendukung pendapat tersebut dengan beberapa argumen.

Social Function

To persuade readers that an issue is important or that the writer’s opinion is reasonable.

Fungsi sosialnya adalah meyakinkan pembaca bahwa suatu isu penting atau bahwa pendapat penulis masuk akal.

When Do We Use Analytical Exposition?

menyampaikan pendapat tentang isu sosial;
menjelaskan mengapa suatu hal penting;
membangun argumen dengan alasan;
memengaruhi pembaca agar mempertimbangkan sudut pandang kita;
membahas pro dan kontra suatu topik secara kritis;
memberikan rekomendasi yang bertanggung jawab.

Difference from Other Text Types

Text TypeMain PurposeExample Topic
NarrativeTo entertain and teach a moral lessonA legend about honesty
DescriptiveTo describe a person, place, or thingMy school canteen
RecountTo retell past experiencesMy first online shopping experience
ProcedureTo explain stepsHow to check a safe online shop
Analytical ExpositionTo argue that an opinion is reasonableStudents should learn financial literacy

ReiterationRestates opinionTherefore…, In conclusion…, For these reasons…Therefore, students should use money wisely.Oleh karena itu, siswa harus menggunakan uang dengan bijak.

Incorrect: Because the shipping cost is high, therefore I cancel my order.
Correct: Because the shipping cost is high, I cancel my order. / The shipping cost is high; therefore, I cancel my order.

Model Texts with Annotation

Baca empat model teks. Perhatikan thesis, arguments, reiteration, dan bahasa argumennya.

Model Text 1: Teenagers Should Learn Financial Literacy Early

Thesis

I believe teenagers should learn financial literacy early because they make money decisions almost every day. Even if they do not have a job yet, many students already manage pocket money, buy internet data, and decide whether to save or spend. In island communities, these decisions can be more challenging because some items are more expensive due to shipping costs.

Argument 1

First, financial literacy helps students separate needs from wants. A student may need a notebook, internet data for learning, or money for transportation. However, a new phone case, game top-up, or unnecessary online item may only be a want. When students understand this difference, they can make wiser choices.

Argument 2

Second, financial literacy helps teenagers avoid impulsive spending. Some students buy things because their friends have them or because online advertisements look interesting. As a result, they may spend their money too quickly and cannot buy something more important later.

Argument 3

Third, financial literacy protects students from digital risks. Online shopping and digital wallets are useful, but they also require careful thinking. Students need to check sellers, read product reviews, compare total prices, and avoid suspicious links. They must not share OTP codes or passwords with anyone.

Reiteration

Therefore, financial literacy is not only for adults. Teenagers also need it because they already face real money decisions. By learning financial literacy early, students can become more responsible, careful, and confident in managing their money.

What Can We Learn?

This text teaches us that financial literacy helps teenagers make better choices. It also shows that students in island areas need to consider shipping costs, internet access, and digital safety.

Language Features

  • Mental verb: I believe
  • Causal conjunction: because
  • Result connector: As a result
  • Modality: need to, must
  • Evaluative language: useful, careful, responsible

Comprehension Questions

  1. What is the writer’s opinion?
  2. Why do teenagers need financial literacy?
  3. What is the difference between needs and wants?
  4. Why can impulsive spending be harmful?
  5. What digital risks are mentioned in the text?

Think Like a Smart Buyer

Ketika membaca teks berikutnya, perhatikan bahwa harga barang bukan satu-satunya hal yang perlu dipikirkan. Untuk siswa kepulauan, total cost dapat berubah karena shipping cost dan delivery time.

Useful question: Is it still cheap after shipping?

Model Text 2: Online Shopping Is Useful but Risky for Students

Thesis. In my opinion, online shopping is useful for students, but it can also be risky if students are not careful. Many students like online shopping because it offers many choices and sometimes lower prices. However, students must think critically before buying anything online.

Argument 1. First, online shopping can help students find school needs more easily. For example, a student may buy a dictionary, a notebook, or a simple learning tool from an online shop. This can be helpful, especially when the item is not available in a small island store.

Argument 2. Second, students must check the total price before buying. A product may look cheap at first, but the shipping cost to an island area can be expensive. As a result, the total cost may be higher than buying the item in a local shop. Students should compare prices before checkout.

Argument 3. Third, online shopping can be risky because not all sellers are honest. Some shops use attractive pictures, but the real product may be different. Some fake shops may even disappear after receiving payment. Therefore, students need to check ratings, reviews, and seller information.

Reiteration. For these reasons, online shopping is not completely bad, but students must be smart buyers. They should buy only what they need, check the total cost, and avoid suspicious sellers.

Comprehension Questions

  1. Why do many students like online shopping?
  2. Why can shipping cost be a problem for island students?
  3. What should students check before checkout?
  4. Why are product reviews important?
  5. What does “smart buyer” mean in the text?

Model Text 3: Digital Wallets Can Help Students, but They Need Control

Thesis. I think digital wallets can help students, but they need to be used with self-control. A digital wallet can make payment faster and easier. However, it can also make students spend money without thinking carefully.

Argument 1. First, digital wallets are practical. Students can use them to buy internet data, pay for small items, or receive money from family members. In some island areas where access to banks or ATMs is limited, digital payment can be helpful when the internet connection is available.

Argument 2. Second, digital wallets can help students track their transactions. If students check their payment history, they can see where their money goes. This habit can help them understand their spending patterns and make better decisions.

Argument 3. However, digital wallets also have disadvantages. Because payment feels quick and easy, students may spend money too often. They may buy snacks, game top-ups, or online items without realizing how much money they have used. As a result, their balance can disappear quickly.

Argument 4. Moreover, digital wallets require digital safety. Students must protect their passwords and OTP codes. They should not click suspicious links or trust messages that promise free balance. In my opinion, using a digital wallet without digital safety knowledge is dangerous.

Reiteration. Therefore, digital wallets can be useful for students, but they should be used wisely. Students need self-control, spending limits, and digital safety awareness before using them.

Comprehension Questions

  1. What is the writer’s position?
  2. Mention two benefits of digital wallets.
  3. Why can digital wallets encourage impulsive spending?
  4. What should students protect when using digital wallets?
  5. Do you agree with the writer? Why?

Model Text 4: Students Must Be Careful with Digital Scams

Thesis. I believe students must be careful with digital scams because many online criminals target young users. Teenagers often use social media, online shops, and digital wallets. As a result, they may receive fake links, false giveaways, or messages asking for personal data.

Argument 1. First, digital scams can look very convincing. A scammer may pretend to be a seller, a bank officer, or a digital wallet service. The message may say that the student wins a prize or has a problem with an account. Because the message sounds urgent, some students may panic and follow the instruction.

Argument 2. Second, students must understand that OTP codes and passwords are private. No real officer, seller, or friend should ask for them. If students share an OTP code, someone may take over their account. Consequently, their balance or personal data can be stolen.

Argument 3. Third, students should build safe digital habits. They need to check links, read messages carefully, use strong passwords, and ask adults when they are unsure. In island communities, where digital access may be limited and not everyone has the same experience with online safety, sharing knowledge with friends and family is also important.

Reiteration. Therefore, digital safety is part of financial literacy. Students must be careful, calm, and critical when they receive suspicious online messages. Protecting money also means protecting personal data.

Comprehension Questions

  1. Why must students be careful with digital scams?
  2. What kinds of fake messages are mentioned?
  3. Why is sharing OTP dangerous?
  4. What safe habits should students build?
  5. How is digital safety connected to financial literacy?
G

Main Reading Text: Should Students Use Digital Wallets at School?

Baca teks utama dengan teliti. Tandai thesis, argument, dan reiteration.

Paragraph 1 — Thesis
I believe students may use digital wallets for school-related needs, but they must use them wisely. Digital wallets are becoming more common among teenagers. Some students use them to buy internet data, pay for online learning tools, or receive money from their parents. However, digital wallets can also create problems if students do not understand financial literacy and digital safety.

Paragraph 2 — Argument 1: Practical Use
First, digital wallets can make some payments easier. A student may need to buy internet data quickly before joining an online class or sending an assignment. In some cases, digital wallets help students pay without carrying cash. This can be practical, especially when the student is far from a bank or ATM.

Paragraph 3 — Argument 2: Island Context
Second, digital wallets can be helpful for students in island areas. Some families may send money digitally when students need school supplies or transportation. If the internet connection is available, a digital wallet can save time. However, students still need to check their balance and use the money only for important needs.

Paragraph 4 — Argument 3: Spending Risk
Third, digital wallets can make spending feel too easy. When students pay with cash, they can see the money leaving their hands. With digital wallets, the payment happens quickly. As a result, students may not realize how much they have spent. They may buy snacks, game top-ups, or unnecessary online items again and again.

Paragraph 5 — Argument 4: Peer Influence
Another problem is peer influence. Some students may use digital wallets because their friends use them. They may feel left behind if they cannot pay digitally or join online trends. In my opinion, students should not use digital wallets only to look modern. They should use them only when they understand the benefits and risks.

Paragraph 6 — Argument 5: Digital Scams
Digital wallets also require safety awareness. Students may receive fake messages, suspicious links, or false prize announcements. Some scammers ask for OTP codes or passwords. This is dangerous because personal data and balance can be stolen. Therefore, students must learn not to share private codes with anyone.

Paragraph 7 — Reiteration
In conclusion, digital wallets can be useful for students, but they are not just simple payment tools. They require financial literacy, self-control, and digital safety. Students should be allowed to use digital wallets for important needs only if they can manage their spending and protect their accounts.

Your essay should have 4–5 paragraphs, 250–350 words, thesis, arguments, reiteration, at least 5 causal conjunctions, at least 4 mental verbs/opinion expressions, at least 3 finance vocabulary items, and context from student life or island communities.

Pro-Con Table

Pros of Digital WalletsCons of Digital Wallets
Payment is faster.Students may spend money too quickly.
Students can buy internet data easily.Scammers may send fake links.
Parents can transfer money for school needs.Students may forget to check their balance.

Thesis Sentence Bank

I believe students should use digital wallets carefully because they can be useful but risky.
In my opinion, digital wallets can help students if they have financial literacy.
I argue that students should not use digital wallets without self-control and digital safety knowledge.
From my perspective, digital wallets are practical, but students need clear spending limits.

Draft Example

Revised Draft

I believe digital wallets can be useful for students, but they must be used wisely. Many students use digital wallets to buy internet data, school supplies, or online items. This tool is practical because payment can be faster and easier. However, students need financial literacy before using it.

First, digital wallets can support school needs. For example, a student may need internet data to send assignments or join an online class. In island areas, digital payment can also help when access to banks or ATMs is limited. Therefore, digital wallets can be beneficial if students use them for important needs.

However, digital wallets can also encourage impulsive spending. Because payment feels quick, students may buy snacks, game top-ups, or unnecessary online items without thinking carefully. As a result, their balance may disappear quickly. I realize that this problem can happen when students do not set a spending limit.

Moreover, digital wallets require digital safety awareness. Students must not share OTP codes, passwords, or personal data. They should also avoid suspicious links and fake giveaways. In my opinion, digital wallets are dangerous if students use them without understanding online scams.

In conclusion, students may use digital wallets, but they need self-control, spending limits, and digital safety knowledge. Digital wallets are not only about fast payment; they are also about responsibility.

Deep Grammar Lab

Grammar lab ini membantu kamu menulis argumen yang jelas dan tidak asal sambung kalimat.

Lab 1 — because vs therefore

Because introduces a reason. Therefore introduces a result.

Correct: Students need financial literacy because they make money decisions.
Correct: Students make money decisions; therefore, they need financial literacy.

  1. Students should check reviews ________ some sellers are not honest.
  2. The shipping cost is expensive; ________, I will not buy the item.
  3. I need internet data ________ I have an online assignment.
  4. The link is suspicious; ________, we should not click it.
  5. Students should save money ________ school needs are important.

Lab 2 — so vs as a result

So is common in simple cause-effect sentences. As a result sounds more formal and useful in analytical exposition.

Example: The seller has bad reviews, so I will not buy the item.
Formal: The seller has bad reviews. As a result, I will not buy the item.

  1. I spent all my money, so I cannot buy internet data.
  2. The shop has many bad reviews, so students should be careful.
  3. She shared her OTP, so her account was taken over.
  4. He bought unnecessary items, so he had no savings.
  5. The shipping cost is high, so the item is expensive.

Lab 3 — due to vs because

Because is followed by a clause. Due to is followed by a noun phrase.

I canceled the order because the shipping cost was high.
I canceled the order due to the high shipping cost.

  1. Due to the expensive shipping cost, I canceled the order.
  2. Students need self-control because digital wallets are easy to use.
  3. Due to bad reviews, we should not buy from the seller.

Lab 4 — should, must, need to

should = suggestion. need to = necessity. must = strong rule.

  1. Students ________ not share OTP codes.
  2. Students ________ compare prices before checkout.
  3. Teenagers ________ learn financial literacy.

Common Mistakes

MistakeIncorrectCorrectExplanation
Using because and therefore togetherBecause it is risky, therefore I avoid it.Because it is risky, I avoid it.Jangan memakai because dan therefore sekaligus.
Weak thesisDigital wallet is good.I believe digital wallets are useful, but students must use them carefully.Thesis harus jelas dan spesifik.
Opinion without reasonI agree with digital wallets.I agree with digital wallets because they help students pay quickly.Pendapat perlu alasan.
Wrong expressionI very agree.I strongly agree.“I very agree” tidak tepat.
Unnatural phraseAccording to me, …In my opinion, …Gunakan “In my opinion”.
Subject-verb errorDigital wallet make payment easy.Digital wallets make payment easy.Subject plural memakai verb dasar.
Missing reiterationEssay ends after arguments.Therefore, students should use digital wallets wisely.Analytical exposition perlu penegasan ulang.
